This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Esenboğa Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=ltac

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Updated model runs and official observations through the afternoon will determine final resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent monsoon activity and widespread cloud cover across Uttar Pradesh have kept daytime highs in Lucknow suppressed below the September climatological average of roughly 33°C. Official India Meteorological Department guidance and multiple forecast models indicate a maximum near 30–31°C today amid patchy rain or thundershowers, with high humidity and easterly winds limiting solar heating. These conditions align with the market’s heaviest weighting on 31°C (55%) followed by 32°C and 30°C, reflecting trader consensus that ongoing precipitation will prevent temperatures from reaching 33°C or higher. Updated model runs and evening observations will determine final resolution.

Uncertainty remains low because resolution depends on verified maximum observations, likely from the Israel Meteorological Service; any late-day model adjustments or microclimate variations at official stations could still nudge the outcome between 31–33°C, but consensus data currently anchor probabilities tightly around 32°C.

Recent model runs and observations from September 3 (peaks near 29–31°C) reinforce expectations of a typical peak near 30°C, with limited upside risk from stronger tropical influences.

Early September climatology shows average highs near 30–32°C as the southwest monsoon weakens, with moderating sea breezes from the Arabian Sea, high humidity near 60–80%, and variable cloud cover limiting radiative heating. No heatwave or clear-sky intensification is expected, keeping extremes above 33°C at low probability while supporting the tight clustering around 31–32°C. Updated model runs and official briefings through the day will refine these trader-implied odds.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Istanbul Airport in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=LTFM

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from major models, including GFS and ECMWF runs updated September 4, point to a daily maximum near 27°C in Istanbul on September 5 under mostly clear skies and moderate northeasterly winds. These conditions favor strong daytime heating from September solar insolation while the prevailing flow off the Black Sea limits extreme warming, aligning with the market's strong preference for 27°C or 26°C outcomes. Historical early-September averages hover around 25–28°C, and current high-pressure subsidence with minimal cloud cover supports the tight clustering of implied probabilities around these values. Traders appear to weigh the consensus maximum against minor model spread and potential for slight cooling if winds strengthen overnight.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus for the highest temperature in Kuala Lumpur on September 5, 2026, centers on 33–35°C, with 34°C carrying the strongest implied probability at 58.5%.** This reflects current forecast guidance from official and model sources showing a typical equatorial high tempered by cloud cover, scattered thunderstorms, and haze.

Kuala Lumpur’s tropical rainforest climate produces afternoon highs usually between 31–35°C in early September, driven by high solar insolation near the equator, light winds, and humidity exceeding 50–70%. On September 5, METMalaysia’s official district forecast lists a maximum of 35°C under “ribut petir di beberapa tempat” (scattered thunderstorms) with morning haze (jerebu). Multiple numerical models align closely: hourly profiles peak near 34–35°C in the early afternoon before convective clouds and brief showers develop, while some guidance caps the day at 32–33°C if thicker cloud or earlier rain suppresses heating.

Recent developments reinforcing this range include persistent regional haze and the approach of inter-monsoon conditions that favor isolated afternoon convection rather than widespread clearing. These factors introduce modest uncertainty—stronger or earlier storms could limit the high to 33°C, while clearer skies or delayed convection could push readings to 35°C. Historical September averages (roughly 32°C) and the absence of extreme heat signals further anchor expectations within the narrow 33–35°C band that dominates market pricing. Updated model runs and the next official briefing remain the key near-term catalysts.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the National Weather Service and private models indicate a high near 79–80°F in Central Park on September 5 under mostly sunny skies and northerly flow behind a weak front. This places the 80–81°F bin as the clear market leader at 56 percent implied probability. Cooler Canadian air and lower dew points are suppressing readings relative to the 84°F expected on September 4 and the early-September climatological normal of roughly 80°F. Model consensus shows little spread, with only minor timing differences in the onshore breeze keeping the 78–79°F outcome at 27.5 percent. No heat-advection signals or model runs support the low-probability 82°F+ bins.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Chicago O'Hare Intl Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=kord

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service forecasts for Chicago on September 5 point to a high in the low-to-mid 80s°F, reflecting a cooling trend after the city’s hottest early-September stretch in over four decades. Northeast winds of 5–10 mph, combined with Lake Michigan moderation, are expected to limit inland peaks while keeping readings near the historical average of roughly 80°F. Model consensus shows limited disagreement, with only modest chances of morning clouds or isolated showers that could cap temperatures. Market-implied odds cluster tightly around 82–85°F because traders weigh these official guidance elements against residual heat and typical lake-breeze variability, underscoring the narrow uncertainty range one day before resolution.

Trader-implied odds remain evenly distributed across 35–43°C because ensemble guidance still shows modest spread from variables such as afternoon boundary-layer mixing, exact timing of any thin high cloud, and local urban heat-island amplification. Official AEMET and ECMWF updates expected in the next 24–48 hours will tighten resolution criteria around the observed daily high, while historical analogs indicate that sustained clear, dry conditions can add 1–2°C relative to guidance.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Amsterdam Airport Schiphol Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eham

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts for Amsterdam on September 6, 2026, indicate a maximum temperature near 20–23 °C under partly cloudy to overcast skies with minimal precipitation risk and light southerly winds. This aligns closely with the 1991–2020 climatological average high of 20.2 °C for the date, supported by a broad high-pressure ridge extending from the Azores region that limits strong warm advection from southern Europe’s ongoing heat dome. Numerical weather prediction models, including ECMWF and GFS runs, show consistent agreement on this mild outcome with little spread in projected maxima. Historical records note an all-time high of 29.4 °C in 2023, but current steering patterns and stable subsidence make such extremes unlikely without a significant forecast shift. Updated model guidance and official KNMI briefings in the next 24–48 hours will refine resolution criteria for the daily maximum.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent southwest monsoon enhancement from Tropical Storm Pilandok, which exited the Philippine Area of Responsibility on September 3, continues to drive cloud cover, scattered thunderstorms, and moderate daytime highs across Metro Manila. Official PAGASA guidance and multiple forecast models indicate September 6 highs near 28–30 °C (82–86 °F) with high humidity and frequent rain, limiting solar heating compared to clearer conditions typical earlier in the season. These factors align with historical early-September patterns under active habagat flow, where afternoon maxima often remain below seasonal peaks. Updated PAGASA bulletins and short-range model runs through September 5 will provide the final observational data for market resolution.
